answer: Anchor each agent identity to a time-locked collateral bond: to join the economy an agent locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. One fake account is cheap, but a Sybil swarm needs one bond per identity, so the attacker's cost scales with every fake node while honest agents pay only the lock-up. The bond's long horizon matters: it cannot be recycled quickly, so the ripple of one detected fraud freezes capital across the whole cluster, making mass fakery uneconomic.
